text: The SCIS vehicle-registration transfer is consumed as an activity on queue rwb-integration with the placeholder for its operation name, call type and answer shape, and is faked until P2 publishes them; no C dependency is claimed because DP-16 is outside the pattern set of this slice.
why: No source gives SCIS a row in TSD S5 T5.1 or an operation name, INT-28 records the interface as not available today, and the pattern set of the story rows carries DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19 only, so the build cannot wait for a name at wave 3.
read: FSD S5 A2.19.2; TSD S5 T5.1 and T-A.1; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 INT-28; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-16
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4028-APP s3, s12.2 and s12.8; RWB-S5-E4028-CON s12.2 and s12.8
confirm: Owner of rwb-integration (P2) at the contract tag of RWB-S5-E4028-CON
impact: One consumed row and one fake carry the placeholder; a published name, call type and answer shape replace them in a minor version, and a C row is added only if the pattern set is revised.

text: The step prepares the transfer pack and submits it through the adapter where the interface answers, and records the officer's submission reference where INT-28 answers that the interface is not available; both paths sit behind the same activity and the same fixture set.
why: The FSD and the features sheet make the step a system submission that runs unattended, while INT-28 records that SCIS is prepared by the officer today; keeping one activity with two documented paths lets the build proceed without deciding a fact that no source states for the target.
read: FSD S5 A1.2 and A2.19; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 features and integrations sheets; legacy RWB-E4-028 AC2
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4028-APP s4 step 5, s7 and s12.8; RWB-S5-E4028-CON s12.2 and s13
confirm: Business analyst and the owner of rwb-integration at the tag of RWB-S5-E4028-CON
impact: One activity, two answers; the acceptance criteria read the accepted answer, and the officer's reference path is covered by the rejected and unavailable cases of the fakes.

text: The vehicle registration particulars and the SCIS submission reference are held with the submission record of the step and are written to no column of rwb_asset, because TSD S5 T3.1 names none.
why: The transfer pack needs the registration particulars and the submission reference, and the data model names neither; adding a column would invent an element the LDM does not carry and would break the rule that no source value is invented.
read: TSD S5 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD S5 A2.19; legacy RWB-E4-028 Data table
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4028-APP s11 and s12.7; RWB-S5-E4028-CON s11 and s12.7
confirm: Solution architect and the DB story of the service at the physical schema review
impact: No migration is written; the particulars and the reference live with the record of the submission and the gap stays open until the LDM names an element.

text: A rejected or unanswered transfer leaves the state, the task and the timer of R-DIS-53 to a later split revision: the step fails closed, records the pack and the answer, raises an alert and moves nothing, and no message is invented for it.
why: R-DIS-53 is in the DISPOSAL rule set and no story row of the split owns it, so implementing TITLE_BLOCKED here would build behaviour no story authorises, while ignoring the rejection would lose the fact.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DIS-53; TSD S5 T4; FSD S5 A2.19.4.3; split plan rows for RWB-E4-028
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4028-APP s4 step 10, s5 X6, s9 and s19; RWB-S5-E4028-CON s14 and s19
confirm: Business analyst and the owner of the DISPOSAL route set at the next split revision
impact: No TITLE_BLOCKED row and no message is built here; the rejection is recorded and alerted, and the story that owns R-DIS-53 adds the state, the task and the timer.

text: The DISPOSAL package is loaded in force through the service template without an H row for RWB-PLT-E1072-CON or a C row for RWB-P7-E1073-CON in this slice, because DP-04 is outside the pattern set of the story rows.
why: The patterns of the slice are DP03, DP05, DP13 and DP19, which add only the decision-record and composite-route rows, and no source says which pattern carries the package load.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; story row patterns; FSD S5 A2.19.3.1; TSD S5 T4
applied_in: RWB-S5-E4028-APP s3 and s13; RWB-S5-E4028-CON s4, s8 and s13
confirm: Solution architect at the pattern-set review of the service
impact: The dependency row of the story is unchanged; a later pattern revision may add the platform row.

text: The slice traces to BR-029 of the Epic 4 BRD and names REQ-S5-008 with the collision stated, while the PRD reference stays Pending (C1) and the story row keeps its empty requirement list.
why: BR-029 cites REQ-S5-008 for FEAT-AST-19 and FEAT-AST-20 while TSD S5 T8 maps the same id to FEAT-AST-08, and the split plan carries no requirement id for this slice, so the trace must state both readings and invent no id.
read: TSD S5 T8; Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-029; story rows with reqs []
confirm: Business analyst when the PRD of S5 allocates requirement ids
impact: Traceability rows name BR-029 and REQ-S5-008 with the collision; no requirement row is added to the metadata table.
